rationale: The hypothesis posits that serial MRI differentiates PLAA-related disorder from classical ZNHIT3-associated PEHO syndrome because PLAA shows an initially preserved cerebellum in neonates while ZNHIT3 causes congenital cerebellar hypoplasia at birth. However, the literature refutes both premises: first, patients with PLAA pathogenic variants (e.g., c.68G>T, p.Gly23Val) have documented cerebellar atrophy and hypoplasia on MRI as early as 14 days of life. Second, classical ZNHIT3-associated PEHO syndrome is pathologically and radiologically defined by severe progressive, postnatal cerebellar atrophy (specifically degeneration and loss of cerebellar granule neurons) rather than congenital cerebellar hypoplasia present at birth.

evidence.text: In a cohort of patients presenting with PEHO and PEHO-like phenotypes, a patient harboring a pathogenic PLAA variant (c.68G>T, p.Gly23Val) showed cerebellar hypoplasia and atrophy on brain MRI at only 14 days of age, contradicting the idea that PLAA cases have an initially preserved neonatal cerebellum.

new_directions.question_text: Can volumetric quantitative MRI of the brainstem versus cerebellar cortex differentiate PLAA-associated neurodegeneration from ZNHIT3-associated granule neuron degeneration in the first 6 months of life?
new_directions.rationale: Since qualitative assessment of cerebellar volume loss shows extensive overlap between early-infantile PLAA and ZNHIT3 cases, quantitative volumetric ratios between supratentorial structures, pons, and cerebellar subregions may reveal distinct patterns of progression.

new_directions.question_text: Do early extra-neurological features (such as transient subcutaneous edema characteristic of classical PEHO) reliably separate ZNHIT3 variants from PLAA variants before neuroimaging changes become distinct?
new_directions.rationale: Edema of the face and limbs is a cardinal defining feature in PEHO criteria that is frequently absent or inconsistent in PEHO-like disorders caused by other genes including PLAA.
